title: Emergency: reserved-pool undersubscription causes burst fallback failures; hotfix deployed
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Summary: On 2025-11-20 multiple customers reported sustained 429/503 errors during burst periods despite reserved pools showing available GPUs. Investigation found an undersubscription condition in the autoscaler path that prevented timely burst allocation and forced fallback to lower-tier model variants, causing visible latency and quality regressions for customers using dedicated capacity. Scope: impacts reserved-pool autoscaling decisions for Dedicated customers using burst windows and headroom-based signals. Affected subsystems: reserved-pool allocator, burst headroom estimator, allocation token lifecycle, and the fallback routing policy. Root cause (short): a race condition combined with an inverted metric in the headroom estimator led to the autoscaler treating available capacity as negative headroom in a narrow timing window. That incorrect signal suppressed new node provisioning for 30-90s during high-concurrency bursts. Additionally, a token reuse bug caused the allocator to skip reconciliation for some tenants when a transient API error occurred.

Steps to reproduce: 1) Create a reserved pool with burst enabled and a small headroom (1-2 GPUs). 2) Replay concurrency pattern from customer workload (spiky arrivals, median seq len 400). 3) Observe allocator logs: headroom_estimate reported negative and no scale-up decision for ~30s despite queue growing. 4) Reproduce token reuse path by simulating transient 503 on allocation request; allocator marks tenant reconciled incorrectly.

Immediate mitigation: rolled out a conservative guard in the autoscaler to treat any negative headroom as zero and add a 10s minimum re-eval window; added a retry backoff for allocation tokens to avoid premature reconcile marking. Deployed hotfix ring to prod on 2025-11-24 (dedicated-autoscaler-2025.11.2).

Longer-term actions: - Replace the heuristic headroom estimator with a probabilistic estimator that surfaces confidence bands and ties into the autoscaler decision weight. - Add end-to-end integration tests for the token lifecycle, including simulated transient infra errors. - Improve observability: add headroom_confidence and token_state metrics, new dashboard panels, and an alert when reconciliation loops exceed expected latency. - Postmortem and customer comms (see comments).
comments: 2025-11-20 09:12 - Ava Martinez: Initial customer report from Acme Health: sustained 429s during scheduled business-hour burst. Reproduced locally with workload harness. Escalating to on-call infra and platform owners.

2025-11-20 11:03 - Ravi Patel (on-call): Dug into allocator logs. Found repeated 'headroom_estimate=-4' messages followed by no scale_up decision. Allocator had a fast path that early-exited if token state == 'reconciled', and we saw token flips after transient API 503s.

2025-11-20 14:27 - Lila Chen (SRE): Added temporary alert rule: alert when reserved_pool_scaleup_attempts == 0 AND request_queue_growth > 0 for >15s. Triggered for two customers during today's burst. Pager notified infra leads.

2025-11-21 08:45 - Ravi Patel: Hypothesis: metric inversion in headroom estimator introduced in runtime-1.20 change (PR #2567) where percentile sign was flipped. Reproduced with unit test. Preparing rollback vs hotfix discussion with PMs.

2025-11-21 12:00 - Mia Alvarez (PM): Customer impact high. We should prioritize a hotfix rather than rollback to avoid collateral changes. PM recommendation: hotfix that is conservative + patch to token lifecycle and postmortem follow-ups.

2025-11-22 09:30 - DevTeam: Hotfix implemented: (a) clamp headroom to >=0 before decision, (b) add 2-phase token reconcile with exponential backoff for transient errors, (c) instrumented headroom_confidence metric. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/2783
2025-11-23 16:10 - QA: Integration test added to harness to simulate 503 during allocation and spiky arrival pattern. Automated regression passed on staging. Staging perf: no 429s in 30 runs.

2025-11-24 02:05 - Ravi Patel: Deployed hotfix to 10% canary, monitored metrics for 1 hour — headroom_estimate stabilized and scale-ups triggered as expected. No customer-facing errors observed in canary tenants.
2025-11-24 06:50 - SRE: Increased canary to 50% and then full rollout completed by 11:00. On-call notes: no recurrence in subsequent bursts. Will keep enhanced alerting for 7 days.

2025-11-25 09:00 - Customer Success (Jordan Ross): Sent templated comms to affected customers explaining root cause, short-term fix, and roadmap for permanent mitigations. Received acknowledgement from Acme Health and two other customers. Offer made for credits for incurred errors.

2025-11-26 15:30 - Research/Applied ML (Priya Singh): Model of headroom estimator being replaced with probabilistic model. Tracking work in a separate ticket PM-4021. Will coordinate to align rollout with autoscaler changes.

2025-11-27 10:12 - Ravi Patel: Post-deploy checks green. Closing incident and moving remaining items to backlog: longer-term estimator rewrite, runbook updates, SLA adjustments for micro-burst windows. Action items assigned below.
